_source:
A real 'Travel and Tourism Form 2 Scheme of Work' (a real Zambian secondary school's own department) was shared with this project via Drive, across a standalone Term 1 document, a standalone Term 2 document, and a combined Term 1-3 document. A teacher's name and school name were found in the header of every one of these documents and are not reproduced here per this app's standing sourcing policy. This is a genuine gap fill -- this app previously had no Travel and Tourism Form 2 content at all (only Form 1 Terms 2-3). Cites the real official '2024 Travel and Tourism Syllabus, Ordinary Secondary Education Form 1-4' with real page citations (pp.21-28).

The standalone Term 1 and Term 2 documents and the combined Term 1-3 document carry the same real content for Terms 1 and 2 (the combined document is simply a re-export of the same two standalone documents plus a real Term 3 section, so no separate Term 1/Term 2 duplicate count applies beyond the file-level re-upload itself).

A genuine structural feature of the source is preserved rather than silently corrected: sub-topic 2.3.1 'Intermediaries in the Tourism Industry' is introduced in the final week of Term 1 and its skill-demonstration practice continues into the first week of Term 2 -- this file places the whole of Topic 2.3 under Term 1 (matching the source's own Term 1 revision block, which explicitly names its scope as 'Topics 2.1 - 2.3'), with the Term 2 week 1 continuation folded into the same sub-topic's competencies rather than duplicated as a separate topic entry.

Term 3 is a genuine content gap, not fabricated: the real combined Term 1-3 document's own Term 3 section (all 9 teaching weeks) is headed 'DEEPENING & APPLICATION' and consists entirely of mastery/application activities applying Topics 2.1-2.5 already covered in Terms 1-2 (comparing Zambian destinations with the SADC region, developing a business plan for a tourism intermediary), plus revision and End of Year Examinations -- it introduces no new numbered syllabus topic of its own, consistent with the official syllabus's own Topics 2.1-2.5 being the full scope of new Form 2 content. No separate Term 3 topic is invented here to fill that real gap.

Its own Content/Concept, Learning Activities, Strategies/Methods and Materials/Resources columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for every other bundled subject in this app.

subject.name: Travel and Tourism
subject.description: Travel and Tourism syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre, 2024).

grade.name: Form 2
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 2" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1 Tourism Destination and Attractions in Zambia
sub_topics.description: Locating Zambia's tourism regions and analysing natural and man-made attraction centres and their economic contribution.

competencies.description: Locate tourism regions (South West/Lusaka/Central/Eastern, Copperbelt/North-Western, Northern/Muchinga/Luapula) and the factors that make a destination attractive
Analyse natural and man-made attraction centres and their contribution to the local and national economy

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1 Destination Planning
sub_topics.description: Tourism destination planning: key components, steps, and creating a marketing campaign for a destination.

competencies.description: Plan tourism destination packages, including their key components, the steps involved, and a marketing campaign (branding, promotional materials, strategy)

sub_topics.name: 2.2.2 Carrying Capacity
sub_topics.description: The concept, types, and factors affecting carrying capacity; the dangers of exceeding it, and how to manage it sustainably.

competencies.description: Assess the carrying capacity of tourism destinations, and design a sustainable tourism management plan to manage it (visitor limits, off-season travel, infrastructure)

sub_topics.name: 2.3.1 Intermediaries in the Tourism Industry
sub_topics.description: Identifying intermediaries (travel agents, tour operators), their functions and drawbacks, and demonstrating the skills used in travel agency operations, job opportunities, and the tourism value chain. This sub-topic's practice continues from its introduction in the final week of Term 1 into the first week of Term 2 in the source scheme.

competencies.description: Identify intermediaries in the tourism industry (travel agents, tour operators), analyse their functions, and discuss their drawbacks
Demonstrate skills used in travel agency operations (guidance, itinerary, package, reservations), explore related job opportunities, and draw the tourism value chain

sub_topics.name: 2.4.1 Seasonality in Tourism
sub_topics.description: Concepts, functions, causes and types of seasonality (peak, off, shoulder season); measures to overcome it and planning events and tours accordingly.

competencies.description: Plan events and tours according to seasons, applying measures to overcome seasonality (creating seasonal tour packages, off-season or shoulder-season events)

sub_topics.name: 2.5.1 Impacts of Tourism
sub_topics.description: Positive impacts (economic benefits, cultural exchange) and negative impacts (environmental degradation, overcrowding, cultural commodification) of tourism, and measures to mitigate the negative impacts.

competencies.description: Manage the impacts of tourism by applying measures to mitigate negative impacts (responsible travel behaviour, community-based tourism, environmental conservation)
